updates.name: Suzanne M. Remillard
updates.bio: Andrews Forest LTER information manager in Oregon State University's Forest Ecosystems and Society department, a post the ORCID record lists from 2005. Earlier roles were natural resource database manager at the USDA Forest Service Pacific Northwest Research Station and computer specialist at the USGS Forest and Rangeland Ecosystem Science Center.
updates.research_interests: ecological database design; ecological metadata; database management; forest ecosystems; natural resources
updates.current_affiliation: Forest Ecosystems and Society, Oregon State University

updates.name: Eric-Preston Hamren
updates.bio: Nursery manager at Hakalau Forest National Wildlife Refuge on Hawai‘i Island. A 2025 Hawai‘i Public Radio report says the refuge nursery, after a year and a half of work, was getting its first plants ready for replanting in the forest, with a goal of 30,000 plants a year.
updates.evidence: He's back in his role as nursery manager
updates.notes: Only source is a news article (HPR, 2025-11-20) that names the role and the nursery's work; no USFWS staff profile could be located (session web-search budget was exhausted before an agency page search). No homepage, ORCID or Scholar link found. Verifier: bio no longer calls those plants 'native' (the article says so only of the greenhouse as a whole).

updates.name: Dolan Eversole
updates.bio: Coastal Processes Specialist with UH Sea Grant (University of Hawai‘i), coordinating Waikīkī Beach management in partnership with the beach's Special Improvement District Association. A coastal geologist with UH Mānoa geology degrees, Eversole was NOAA Coastal Storms Program regional coordinator for the U.S.-affiliated Pacific Islands (2010–2015) and advised the state DLNR coastal lands office (2003–2010).
updates.research_interests: coastal hazard mitigation; coastal management policy; coastal ecosystem conservation; emergency management; adaptation to shifting weather
updates.current_affiliation: University of Hawai‘i Sea Grant College Program
updates.notes: Existing homepage (UH Sea Grant directory detail) fetched 200 and carries the bio text. The HISSC coordinator role in current_affiliations comes from the HISSC project page and is not restated on the profile. No ORCID or Google Scholar link on the profile. Verifier: 'climate adaptation' replaced with the page's wording; these interests are the coastal issues the profile names for the DLNR advisory work.

updates.name: Aimee Sato
updates.bio: Indigenous Stewardship Specialist and Stewardship Coordinator at the Hawai‘i Institute of Marine Biology, serving the He‘eia National Estuarine Research Reserve. Holds a UH Mānoa botany MS focused on biocultural restoration of Hawaiian dry forests, and works to connect conservation, science and community, supporting ‘āina-based conservation and co-developed research grounded in Native Hawaiian values.
updates.research_interests: biocultural restoration; traditional ecological knowledge; community-based conservation; cultural ecosystem services; botany; plural ways of knowing
updates.current_affiliation: He‘eia National Estuarine Research Reserve, Hawai‘i Institute of Marine Biology, University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa
updates.notes: HIMB profile links Google Scholar user=gcmub3UAAAAJ ('Publications (Google Scholar)'); scholar.google.com itself not fetched. Note: heeianerr.org/about-us/ currently lists her as 'Biocultural Research & Administrative Assistant', which differs from the HIMB title; the HIMB individual profile was used. No ORCID found.

updates.name: Fred Reppun
updates.bio: Assistant Specialist and Education Coordinator at the Hawai‘i Institute of Marine Biology, leading education and outreach for the He‘eia National Estuarine Research Reserve, including teacher training in ‘āina-based education. Trained in environmental science and policy with an agroecosystem science focus, he co-manages reserve internships and fellowships and represents HIMB on the Kāne‘ohe Bay Regional Council.
updates.research_interests: place-based (‘āina-based) environmental education; teacher professional development; agroecosystem science; soil and water resource management
updates.current_affiliation: He‘eia National Estuarine Research Reserve, Hawai‘i Institute of Marine Biology, University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa

updates.name: Mark Green
updates.bio: Senior Research Associate in Case Western Reserve University's Department of Earth, Environmental and Planetary Sciences, studying how forests regulate the water cycle and what that means for ecosystem energy, carbon and nutrient budgets, mostly through data-intensive analysis. Under a joint venture, also serves as Research Hydrologist at Hubbard Brook Experimental Forest, run by the U.S. Forest Service.
updates.research_interests: forest controls on the water cycle; ecosystem energy, carbon and nutrient budgets; how forests respond to climate change, natural variability and management; data-intensive analysis
updates.current_title: Senior Research Associate; Research Hydrologist, Hubbard Brook Experimental Forest
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Earth, Environmental and Planetary Sciences, Case Western Reserve University

Project site greenmarkb.com did not resolve.

updates.name: Matthew Ayres
updates.bio: Professor of Biological Sciences at Dartmouth, also associate director of its Institute of Arctic Studies and co-chair of its graduate program in ecology, evolution, environment and society. Studies insect population ecology, especially forest pests, seeking the forces that drive some species to high, sharply fluctuating abundance while keeping most populations stable.
updates.research_interests: population ecology; physiological ecology; forest insects and pests; forest ecology and management; climate change ecology
updates.current_title: Professor of Biological Sciences; Associate Director, Institute of Arctic Studies
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Biological Sciences, Dartmouth College
updates.notes: Hubbard Brook people page links ORCID 0000-0001-6120-9068; pub.orcid.org record name Matthew Ayres, employment Dartmouth College Biological Sciences, Professor (1993-present), consistent. Dartmouth biology profile (200 via curl; WebFetch rejected its certificate) and faculty-directory.dartmouth.edu/matthew-p-ayres carry the same biography. The profile is written in the first person; no pronoun used.

updates.name: Melany Fisk
updates.bio: Professor at Miami University (Biology; Institute for the Environment and Sustainability) and a forest ecosystem scientist. The group studies how plants and soil microbes respond to interactions among nitrogen, phosphorus, calcium and carbon, to understand what controls forest productivity and how environmental change may affect it.
updates.research_interests: interactions among nitrogen, phosphorus, calcium and carbon in forests; plant and microbial nutrient responses; limits on forest productivity; environmental change effects on forests
updates.current_affiliation: Biology and Institute for the Environment and Sustainability, Miami University
updates.notes: Hubbard Brook people page links ORCID 0000-0003-4248-0180 and the Miami profile; pub.orcid.org record name Melany Fisk, employment Miami University Biology, Professor (2014-), consistent. Profile is first person; no pronoun used.
